page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.6 GHz. Equipped with 976 GB of system RAM, it provides a substantial memory ratio of 15.25 GB per vCPU. The instance utilizes the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading enabled, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and AES cryptography. Local storage and GPUs are not bundled with this server type.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong multi-threaded execution and parallel processing capabilities. It achieved strong results in PassMark database operations, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core execution, image processing, ray tracing, and software compilation via Clang. Conversely, single-core CPU metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench sit in the average tier, alongside uncached memory bandwidth (150.66 GB/sec read, 62.1 GB/sec write) and static web serving throughput.

The m3-megamem-64 provides high memory resource density, trading off local storage drive availability and single-threaded velocity for high memory capacity and parallel throughput. This configuration makes it suited for large in-memory databases, memory-bound analytical systems, enterprise software builds, and heavy multi-threaded workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on 32 physical Intel Xeon cores operating at 2.6 GHz, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs and 976 GB of system RAM. With 15.25 GB of RAM per vCPU, 54 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and VAES instruction sets, the instance delivers high memory density without bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing reveals strong performance in multi-core tasks, including PassMark database operations, Geekbench multi-core scoring, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Single-threaded metrics and uncached memory bandwidth fall into the average range for its hardware tier. The instance represents a resource-dense deployment option for workloads where memory capacity and concurrent execution are critical, making it well-matched for large in-memory caching systems, database management systems, batch data processing, and enterprise software backends.
